title: Principles, Laws, Traditions and Commands Part 2
paragraphs: I want to conclude this part by understanding principles, laws, traditions, and commandments. The focus today is on understanding the unique nature of divine law in comparison to principles, precepts, commandments, and traditions. I want to briefly discuss immigration. But I want to discuss it in the light of migration and immigration within the Kingdom. The two words look alike: migration and immigration. Migration involves displacement, where people change location. People migrate from one country to another.

You can migrate from one part of a country to another part of a country. You can migrate from New York to California. However, migration normally refers to changing countries, where you actually migrate from one jurisdiction under a particular government to another. Migration. These two words are used all over the world. Europe. When I was in France, it was mainly about all those people who migrated to France from different countries and tried to impose their culture on French culture.

There was a heated discussion. Germany much fuss over migration, especially. Germany used to be, as you know, divided into East and West Germany. West Germany was more prosperous than East Germany, and when they became one country again, thousands of people began moving from the east to the west, because the east had been communist. So people migrated from the east to the west in search of a better life. Now migration is also taking place here in the Bahamas. People migrate from other countries to the Bahamas.

The Bahamas are a very attractive place. You don't often hear about people migrating to Mexico. You also don't often hear about people migrating to Haiti by the thousands. Think about this for a moment. What you hear is actually the opposite, right? You hear people migrating from Mexico to where? The United States. And they are migrating from Haiti to where? To the Bahamas. Okay. And it concerns many different countries, not just these two. I want to pick these two out because we know them.

Migration is not a random event. People don't migrate just like that. They have a motivation to migrate. You don't often hear of Bahamian residents migrating from the Bahamas. Did you know? We constitute the smallest percentage of migrants in the Caribbean. Bahamian residents stay at home. They are going to study. They can stay there for ten years and then come back. Why? Because somehow we lack the motivation to migrate. I will explain why in a moment. Write this down now. It is very important.

What is the motivation for migration? This is an important question. Why do people move, even if it puts their own lives in danger? Why do people take risks to migrate? What is the motivation for migration? Let me give you a few answers. This is the most important one. I think it is about seeking a better life. Do you agree with that? Absolute. This is the greatest motivation for people to migrate. Some people from the Bahamas migrate to the United States for employment and a better salary.

In other words, the fundamental motivation for migration is the search for a better life. If you ask someone who has migrated to the Bahamas, they will say: "I come here for a better life." Those who migrate to the United States also come for a better life. Some people migrate from the Caribbean to Canada or England. They are looking for only one thing: a better life. You don't migrate to become poorer. What I say is very important.

Secondly, people migrate because they want to benefit from the privileges of a country. Imagine that you live in a country where freedom of movement is restricted or where there is oppression. You migrate to another country because the privileges of freedom, freedom of movement, freedom of business, and freedom of religion are easier to obtain there. So you want to migrate because of the privileges and benefits of a country. A third reason why people migrate is to pursue their personal ambitions.

Imagine this: you have a doctorate and live in a small country where they do not value your substance, knowledge, and experience. So you are migrating because you want to develop yourself personally. So you have a personal ambition to migrate. People also migrate because they want better business opportunities. Perhaps they cannot do business well in their current country, or perhaps the policy is too restrictive for them. So they want to live in a country where they can turn their ideas into a lot of money.

That is ambition. For that reason, they migrate. Number four, and let me just change this. I am going to tell you why people do not migrate. The reason why people do not migrate is because they want to learn the constitution of the country. Is that correct? In other words, the constitution is not the attraction. Those might well be the benefits, but they are not going there because they want to read this document and think the document is good. It is not the constitution that drives them to the country.

Secondly, people do not migrate because they want to understand and abide by the laws of the country. In fact, most people nowadays migrate by breaking the law. They are breaking the law to migrate. They come in through the back door. So people do not come to countries because they want to obey the laws, or because they think the laws are good. They are coming for those three most important reasons. This is very important. And people don't migrate because they want to pay taxes in a country either.

So you know, well, I can't wait to go to that country so I can pay my taxes. You don't say that. In fact, that is the last thing you want to pay when entering a country. You don't want to pay tax. Look at that list. We have three drivers for migration, and they all have to do with personal gain and the pursuit of ambition. But we are not thinking about those other three. I do not change my nationality because I like the laws of a country, or because I want to read them or know what they entail.

I do not change my country because I want to understand the constitution of that country, and I do not change my country because I want to pay taxes to that country. Why is this important? I spoke with a young man. I was in San Antonio, Texas, close to the border with Mexico. This man was clearly Mexican, and I was speaking at a conference there. Afterwards, this young man came up to me, and he was moved by what I had told him. He said to me: "Dr.

Monroe, you know, I came to this country 17 years ago, and I used to live in Wakahaki, Mexico." He said that it was one of those poor areas, a garbage dump, and that my parents had grown up on the garbage dump as children. And he said that one day someone showed him a photo of a beautiful city in America from a magazine. He said: "When I saw the photo, I kept the folded piece of paper, and he had only one wish his whole life: that I would go to that place."

He had grown up on a garbage dump, but he had a photo of the United States, a big city. He said that he didn't even know such a thing existed. But he kept the photo. And he said that it had been his dream his whole life to go to that place in the photo. And he said that circumstances arose that eventually led him to go to northern Mexico to visit his uncle. His uncle lived not far from the border.

And he decided, of course, that he had seen television then and all those things, and he saw a world he had never known, and he saw, you know, cars and trains and all those people who were shopping, and all those commercials for hamburgers and everything. He said that he had almost died because he had grown up on a garbage dump and had seen those photos, and said: "My head was full of that country and I had only one dream. I have to go there."

And he said: "You know, one evening my three friends and I decided that we would make the trip." He said: "We knew that we would probably be chased by dogs. We could probably be shot. We could probably be killed if we tried to climb over that fence." He said: "But the dream was greater than the pain." And he said that at midnight we would pack our little bags, put them on our backpacks, and start the journey to the United States, the dream of that time.

He told me this story, and it came back to me when I thought about this session. He said: "You wouldn't believe what we went through. We had to swim through rivers. We had to walk through, you know, cacti that were full of thorns and stuff. There were snakes. We had to watch out for rattlesnakes." He said: "One evening, one of my friends was bitten and sucked the venom out of his feet." In other words, they endured all of this purely because they wanted to change countries due to the hope they saw.

And he said: "Eventually we came to a point where we saw the fence and we knew that a new world lay behind that fence. We also knew that police officers and immigration officials would drive past that fence every 58 minutes. We had 15 minutes to make it. And he said: 'I stood there and I saw my future. If only I could get over that fence.'" He said that the chance of getting caught was high, because many of his friends had ended up in prison and been sent back. They were not treated well.

He said: 'But the poverty I experienced was worth the risk.'"" And then they saw the lights approaching in the night. They saw the SUV with the police, the border police, and he said that they saw him driving past very slowly. They saw him disappear from sight and counted down. 15 minutes. 1 2 3 go. And they ran to the fence. He says that the fence was full of barbed wire. There were all kinds of metal pieces in it to make it difficult. He said: 'I got cut when I put my hand on it for the first time.

The blood started flowing.' He said: 'I started to flee.' He said: 'Dr. Monroe, what I had to endure to come to this country almost cost me my life.' He said: 'But I remember falling to the ground on the other side of that fence.'" He just fell. He scrambled to his feet, he says, and ran through the bushes. He didn't know where he was. He didn't know where he was going. The only thing he knew was that he had to go north, and he changed countries.

He said: 'I have lived illegally in this country for about eight years and I have worked for all kinds of people, I have done all kinds of odd jobs.' And one of the men I worked with harvesting agricultural products on his farm said that he liked me and that I was a very polite young man. He wanted to sponsor me, and he did, and so I became a citizen. I received my residence permit and my green card, and now I am a citizen. He said: 'You know, my children...

I have a family now and they are at this meeting tonight.' And he introduced me to his children. Beautiful children. He said: 'I met my wife here. She is also Mexican.' He said: 'This is my family.' I thought of that man. He said: "When I came here, I only wanted that photo." That photo I saw in the trash can, the one my friend had brought for me out of an old magazine. He said: "And now I'm in the photo. I 'm really in it." He parked a nice car in front of the hall where we were. He has his own house.

His wife sells small items in and around the house. They have a small shop. And he is building his life. And I thought about it. He did not get there because of President Obama, President Clinton, or President Bush. It was not the president who brought him here. You know, we preach Jesus, not the land. People are not looking for a better president. What are they looking for? A better life. He said: "When I arrived in America, the shock was that I had to learn the law. We do not come to other countries for the law.

We come for a better life." He said: "But I discovered that in order to live in this country, I must obey the laws. And the first law I had to comply with was that I had to reside legally in this country and be sponsored." And then he said: "My children went to school and came home again." And he said: "You know, I did n't speak English very well at first, but I had to learn English, because when you come to a country, you have to speak the language.

" But my children came home and showed me the lesson they had had at school about the Constitution. He said: "I didn't know such a thing existed." And he said: "I watched my children's lesson and it said in big letters: The Constitution is the document containing your rights and privileges as a citizen of this country. Read it. You can live in a country without knowing your rights. You can live in a country without knowing your privileges."

"Wow, that reminds me of that couple who won a boat trip on a cruise and had been on the cruise for seven days. They had brought soft drinks, cookies, and cheese and locked themselves in their cabin, because they thought they had only won the cruise ticket. On the sixth day, the captain asked: 'Why has n't cabin 92 reported in?'" They went to cabin 92. The two sat on the floor smiling and ate daisy cheese and crackers. They were so happy to be on the ship. The captain asked: 'What are you doing here?'

They said: 'Well, you know, we thank God that we are on a cruise. It is a beautiful cruise. You have a beautiful ship. It is a nice cabin, sir.' He said: 'But we didn't see you at the meals. Not at the shows. Not at the banquet. Not at the buffet.' They said: 'Oh no, no, no. We can't afford that.' We were just happy that we had won the tickets for the cargo cruise. And the captain saw that this couple didn't know the fine print on the ticket. So he said: "Show me the tickets for the cruise."

And the lady went to her handbag and took out her two tickets. She said: "Look, we won." We won. We won this. We won this. "And he said: "Uh, may I have them, please?" He took them and turned the page as well. On page two it said: "The holder of this ticket has access to all shows, food, banquets, gyms, everything on board." "And the cruise was over. It is possible to be in the kingdom of God, to live in a little hut somewhere and feast on cheese and crackers. Tell your neighbor today, not me. Do you understand?

You can live in a country and not know the privileges, the rights, and the benefits of that country. That is why the law is so important. He said: "I realized that there was a document with all those promises, but that there was also a law that I had to abide by in order to benefit from those promises." That is what migration is about. I am a citizen of God's kingdom. I entered God's land. I came back home, restored the bond with my country, and we must learn the laws.

First of all, we don't change countries because we want to serve that country, do we? We don't think about serving the country. We just want to go to that country to get a better job, earn more money, build a house, give our children a good education. We want to serve the country. We don't join a country to join the army and die. Everyone who agrees with me? That is not the motivation. Haitians don't come to the Bahamas to join the police and then fight in battle.

You don't go to America to become a soldier and fight in Afghanistan. You do n't think about serving the country. My question is an important one. This is *the* most important question. Why did you enter the kingdom of heaven? Why did you come to the kingdom of God? What is your motivation? Let me read what Jesus said about our motivation. And this is The scripture text we read earlier. Jesus said: "I know why you seek Me." "Take a deep breath. You know, I want Jesus. I want you. He said: Why do you want Me?

I love Jesus. Why do you love Jesus? I want to serve Jesus. Why do you want to serve Jesus? He said: You are not fooling me. I know why you want to come here, to my country. What is the motivation? He said: It is not because of the fish and the bread. What drives someone to change countries? They change because they are looking for bread. They are not sitting on a presidential bench. They are not thinking about the laws you have to obey and all those constitutional matters.

Look, I just need to find a good job, earn some money, buy some food and clothes. That is all. That is why I am here. His explanation to our followers reveals our motivation. Jesus said: "I know why you are looking for me." You are looking for me because of the bread and the fish that I gave you yesterday. Let me ask you a question. Are you interested in the laws of God at all? Or do you just want to receive some food from God? Do you just want to come to that country and get things?

Free healthcare, getting pregnant, free care for the baby. I mean, why are you coming to that country? "He said: " What haven't you done?" You have broken a law. Jesus said: " I know why you follow me." "" Look," said He, "not because you have seen the miraculous signs, but because you have eaten fish sandwiches." "" Oh, he's cool. Hey, he should just shut his mouth. Jesus. No, I have your heart. I know what is going on. Your motivation is not to learn about the kingdom of God.

You do not want to know the laws of the kingdom. You just want something to eat. You do not read the Constitution. How many of you have read the Bible this week and yet you come before God and say: 'Lord, I need a blessing.' I have to pay that energy bill. God said: 'But you have n't even touched the Constitution.' He exposes us. What is your motivation? Migration should go deeper than just benefits. Now look at verse 27. He says: 'Do not work for your food.' Oh no, man. That is the reason to make the trip.

That is why I went by boat. That is why I climbed over the fence. I come here for a good life. He says: 'Do not make the journey for bread.' Do you know what made America great? What has made America a successful nation? You know what? Suppression. The people who traveled from Europe to America were oppressed. They were religiously oppressed and longed for religious freedom. That is why they took the leap across the ocean from England, France, and Spain to reach the promised land, America. Some died along the way.

And they built America on one word: freedom. But look what is happening now. They have no motivation left. So they are mutilating freedom. That is why they were called pioneers. They fought. They fought to subdue the land. They built farms. They moved west. It was hard. They fought against the native population. They had that passion because of the oppression. What motivates us to follow Jesus? Just bread? Food. That spoils. I offer you something that does not spoil: a permanent home. Hallelujah. I offer you life.

Look at this verse. I found it interesting. Matthew 16. He says: "Whoever wants to follow Me must deny himself." " Wait a minute. That is the motivation for coming to the country: to take care of myself." He said: "No, you must come without that being your main motivation, which means that you come for something deeper." You are here for something more important than just the benefits of the law. You are appearing before the law. You come for the life of the country. He says: 'Whoever follows Me must deny himself.'

Take up his cross and follow Me. For whoever wants to save his life, what must he do? Losing. That means that you must give up your personal motivation, your ambitions to enter the Kingdom of God, for the sake of the Kingdom of God. In other words, you come in, someone else already has it. You must come to serve the country, not just so that the country can serve you. Do you understand what I mean?

It is so subtle that we can become motivated by what the country can do for us, that we no longer care about the country. If you stop loving a country, you destroy it. And therefore Jesus said: 'You must come and lose your life.' "We are going to another country to build a life, not to lose a life. We are going to another country to create a life, not to deny a life." His idea is that it is about the country. It is not about your personal ambitions. It is not about your private needs.

It is about serving the laws of the land. To understand the constitutional requirements. In other words, may I put it this way? Privileges and profit in a country should be by-products of obedience to the laws of the land. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness. Justice means obeying the laws, and then all these things, he says, are given to you as well. And what he says is: look, if you come to this country for these things, you are missing the reason for your coming.

Seeking the kingdom means studying the government, studying the constitution, studying the lifestyle, studying the culture, studying the expectations of the kingdom. Study it, learn it, know it, apply it. If you obey the law, the benefits are natural by-products. I am sure that you have all heard of the immigration laws in Arizona. That is a strange law. Everyone is worried about it. "It’s about the law having to do with stopping people on the street.

And if you look like you ’re not a citizen, they can stop you and ask you to show proof. Thank God. God don’t do that. Man, that was a message. Some of you look good right now. We don’t know what’s going on. But this law they passed in Arizona is causing stress, and a lot of ethnic people are moving out of Arizona now because they feel the intimidation is too high. I think the question is: did you come here to Arizona for the food or to obey the laws? If you obey the law and the officer stops you, you smile. Hello.

If you obey the law, you never get intimidated. Oh right. Yes, my card. No problem. But I’m leaving. Arizona says: "Look, the taxes in this state are very low." So you benefit enormously from that. "" Then we got healthcare. We received free education. We got all those things. He said: 'Listen, while you are here, you enjoy all of this, but we want to check if you are obeying the laws.' So they stop you to check if you qualify for the benefits. Let me quote Jesus once again: 'Seek first the kingdom of God.'

That is the country. But then he says: 'And his righteousness. """ That means you need to check your immigration status. Am I obeying the laws? Sometimes you think that God is Santa Claus. But wait a minute. Not even Santa Claus. Because even Santa Claus wants to know if he has been good all year. Some of us have certain rules. You know, if you're good, you get a present. But we think that God is someone who doesn't care about anything. I don't know who we think God is.

You know, it's like we break the law all week and ask God to bless us on the weekend. And then God says: what are you doing? You are either a citizen or you are not a citizen. You always come to me for bread and fish, but you do not submit to the laws of the land. Look at the last part of the verse. He says: 'But whoever wants to save his life will lose it.' Whoever loses his life for me, what will he find? """ When you surrender to the laws of the kingdom of God, you truly have a life. A life. I live.

And God wants you to lead a great life, an abundant life. Life, life. I prophesy that you will be a law-abiding citizen in the kingdom of God this month. And your life structure will change next month. Hallelujah. There is no guesswork about success in life. If you lose your life, He says, for the sake of the land, you will find your life again. Do you know that this is the same? Do you know what the next verse says? Here is a verse right after that. It is verse 26.

It says: 'For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world and loses everything?' "In other words, there are people running around trying to get hold of things, and you know, it’s amazing. You can try to get all those things and lose everything that is important to you. I have seen rich people who are not married. Rich people without children, children who have left home, a boat and a car, and they use them all by themselves. That makes no sense.

You have a ten- bedroom house that you fought for for years, and then you live there alone with the housekeeper. That just makes no sense. You gain the whole world, but lose the things that make life important. It is more important to follow the laws than to earn your living. In Matthew 16:28 it says: 'Truly I tell you, some standing here with me will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming.'" "Isn't that amazing? The same passage. He says: 'This is about the kingdom.'"

You deny yourself so that you can enjoy life in the kingdom. You obey the laws so that you can live in the kingdom. This is how you travel to another country. "My message today is this: You have come into the Kingdom of God to submit to the laws of the land, so that you can benefit from His promises. You do not obey the law to be saved. You obey the law because you are saved. You know, this is funny.

You know, if you are an illegal immigrant and you have been in a country for 25 years, then you have been illegal all that time. In other words, no matter how long you are there, you are still breaking the law. You have been a law-breaking citizen for 25 years. Now pay attention. The moment they naturalize you, you become a naturalized citizen. That means they make you a full-fledged citizen. What happens at that moment? You become a law-abiding citizen.

So for 25 years you were an illegal, law-breaking citizen, even though you lived in that country all those years. But the moment they make you a citizen, that changes. You become a law-abiding citizen. So the question is: why did they give you citizenship? Answer: so that you can obey the law. The reason we are entering the kingdom is so that we can now live legally according to the laws of the God we serve. The message God gives us is: look, I want to bless you. I want to give you prosperity.

I want to grant you a rich life. But you must submit to the laws of the land. Okay. Let me conclude with a few thoughts. We know that God wanted to place us on earth to expand his kingdom, the kingdom of heaven. And he did that because he wanted to establish his culture on earth. He wanted to give us a legal existence on this planet. So the first thing God gave Adam was law. He gave him land and law. Everyone says land and law. Two important L's that you must always remember: land and law.

Where there is land, there must be law. He gave him a garden, gave him the earth, and then he gave him a law. Do not touch that tree. Watch out. The day you eat from it, you will lose your life. That means that before he touched the tree, he was alive. Adam has Such a good life that he has never seen my lips sweat. Now that is what I call a good life. Say amen. Someone, this hits the nail on the head. You know, Reverend Kyle, think about this the next time you give your seminar on financial management.

You only have a good life when you stop sweating. May I say that? I feel a slight anointing here. Do you get it? As long as you are sweating, you do not have a good life yet. I am going to say something. This is a bit profound. Okay, let me give you a hint. People think that a job is hard work. You go to work every morning, you work for someone else, and they pay you. Others think that you are free when you have your own business. Let me tell you something. Look, look, go right ahead with that.

Let me tell you something. When you have your own business, you work twice as hard as when you have a job. I want you to get that insight. So don't think that because I have my own business, I am free now. Right, sister? You work all night long, don't you? While others sleep. But when you have your own business, you no longer work from 9 to 5. You work from 9 to 9 the next morning. That means you sweat twice as hard. It took me years to understand this.

I wondered: "How is it possible that the curse God pronounced on Adam was sweat?" "Sweating, toiling, is not part of the life God envisioned. Okay. So when does someone stop sweating? I’ve figured it out. You know, I’ve studied people like Buffy Gates. These men do n’t sweat. You have to analyze them. I try to work on that myself, too. I try to understand what wealth is. Wealth is n’t work. Wealth is ideas. You are only truly rich when you earn money while you sleep. Bill Gates wakes up every morning.

In fact, while he sleeps, kaching kaching kaching kaching. When you wake up, your bank account rises. He goes straight from bed to the golf course. Kaching, kaching, kaching, kaching there. Kaching. What do they do? Ideas. Adam never broke the law. Whatever you do, listen closely to me. Think quickly about franchising. May I say it again? I just gave you an idea that you can earn millions of dollars with. Let me say it again. Whatever you do, if you are here, you are a beautician."

Stop thinking about running that business. Think about training people to run it while you sleep. That man who owned the insurance company on the boat that was fishing. You still don't get it, do you? You in the field and him at sea. He started selling, you know, he started selling like you, but he had his eye on something else. I think one of the curses of the Bahamas is that we love jobs. Our government is stuck with that problem. I mean, our politicians don't think beyond jobs. So we are in trouble.

If the head gives out, the body does too. God wanted us to govern this beautiful planet without exerting ourselves. But if we break the law, he says: "Then you sweat." Now life is going to be tough. It will be difficult for you to get bread. He says that you will earn your bread with the sweat of your brow. "But remember, he says that you should not work for your bread. He says, and here comes Christ, who contradicts, or rather, tries to correct what happened in the garden.

God says: you shall earn your bread with the sweat of your brow. Christ says: do not work for your bread. In other words, I have come now. I have come to set it right. Glory. Hallelujah. I have come to correct what your forefather did. He broke the law. I have come so that you can obey the law again. And if you obey the law, all these things will be added to you. It does not mean that you should not put effort into life. It means that it should not be a depressing effort. If you hate Mondays, you are toiling.

If you find what you were born for, that is no problem. Then you are in your element, man. You... You are in the zone. You are not sweating in the zone. Can I have an amen? But if you hate getting up on Monday and going to that place to go, yes, then you are toiling. Jesus came to bring you back into the zone. Zoom. And so, someone who does what he or she likes to do, he or she has no trouble with that. They can do it all day long. Never.

But if you hate what you do, or if you have to do it because someone orders you to, then you are a victim of someone else's interests and you are sitting on the toilet. Just go and think about these things. Okay. I want to conclude with: Let's get Psalm 1. Next week we will continue here. Psalm 1. Say to your neighbor: open Psalm 1. Say to your neighbor: obey the law. Open Psalm 1. I learned Psalm 1 when I was three years old. Most of you did. At least the people from Baytown.

This was the most important verse in Sunday school. But I want you to read this verse for the first time in your life. Life. Read it again and read what there stands. Mama Boris, you surely remember this verse. What does the first verse say? Blessed is the man. Pause there for a moment. Do you want to be blessed? The first word in the whole book tells you how you can be blessed. Blessed is the man. Happy and fulfilled is the man who does not walk where the counsel of the wicked.

That word counsel, how do you spell that? Spell it for me. R O U N What? Okay, that means you receive advice from people who are not smart. Whoever gives you advice determines whether you are blessed or cursed. Blessed is the man who walks, who avoids stupid people. I am about to finish, but let me just write this down. In other words, there are people you must avoid. They are bad for your future. You will be blessed. You must choose who you associate with. That is an excellence. No.

Do not stand in the way of the sinners. That does not mean that they walk and you stand. You are in their way. That means that you go where they are. You walk their path. You do what they do, you do what they say. You are with them. You have their lifestyle. You are connected with them. He says: " Blessed is a man who does not engage with the lifestyle of godless people." "" Okay. Blessed is the man who does not walk, who comes from the godly north and lives as a sinner. Now it tells you what you should do.

What is the next verse? But this is their life. Okay? Now you see people thinking that the law is depressing, difficult, you know, full of monotony, that you’re not allowed to do this, not allowed to do that. Listen to me. That is why you are not blessed. If the law is a chain around your neck, if the law is something you hate, then you don't want to do it. It is difficult. It is so difficult.
